reply_text:
I found no dated AI predictions by Ilya Sutskever from 2015, so this counts as a quiet year. All three fixed searches ran as written. I used 9 of my 12 searches and all 6 page openings. One of those openings was wasted: I opened the Interconnects page twice because the first result was cut off in my output.

- **"Introducing OpenAI" (11 December 2015), written by Greg Brockman, Sutskever and the OpenAI team.** I read it in a PDF of the Wayback Machine copy. The post declines to give a date: "it's hard to predict when human-level AI might come within reach." I've listed that under undated because it's about when human-level AI arrives. Note that it's a jointly signed company post, not his words alone. The post's line about spending "a tiny fraction of this in the next few years" is a business forecast, so I left it out.
- **His January 2015 guest post, "A Brief Overview of Deep Learning".** I couldn't open the original blog, so I read a copy reposted on cnblogs on 13 May 2015. It looks ahead only in general terms ("models that do even more computation will probably be very good"), with no date or time span.
- **MIT Technology Review's Innovators Under 35 profile (18 August 2015).** It quotes him saying his translation approach "should beat existing translation technology by a good margin." There's no date attached, and the words come through the profile writer, not a transcript.
- **A 2015 Talking Machines podcast interview.** The transcript on Interconnects (published 2025) is technical and makes no predictions. Its 2015 date comes from the blogger, and I didn't confirm it.
- **Not checked:** a December 2015 RE•WORK question-and-answer interview is on LinkedIn, but the page wouldn't open. I haven't seen its text, so I can't say whether it holds anything.
